title.narrative: Gender-Based Violence – Responding to Critical Gaps for Conflict-Affected Populations in East and Horo Guduru Wollega Zones, Kiremu, Guto Gida, and Jardega Jarte Districts

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThis proposed project responds to the urgent gender-based violence (GBV) needs of women and girls in Kiremu and Guto Gida (East Wollega) zone and Jardega Jarte district (Horo Guduru Wollega zone) severely affected by protracted conflict and insecurity. A targeted needs assessment confirmed a high prevalence of GBV: 24,320 women and girls in Kiremu, 21,142 in Guto Gida, and 25,243 in Jardega Jarte. These figures reflect a deepening protection crisis where conflict, displacement, and the collapse of protection systems have heightened the risk of sexual violence, exploitation, early and forced marriage, and psychological abuse. Access to GBV services remains severely disrupted. The assessment identified major gaps in case management, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services, emergency cash assistance, and operational One-Stop Centers (OSCs). Survivors face limited access to clinical care, legal aid, and psychosocial support due to the lack of trained personnel, safe service points, and functional referral pathways. Without urgent action, thousands will remain unprotected and unsupported. This project proposes a comprehensive, multipile responses aligned with the GBV Area of Responsibility (GBV AoR) 2025 Allocation Strategy. It prioritizes survivor-centered care, integration of services, and local capacity strengthening. The intervention will address immediate needs and contribute to long-term resilience in underserved, high-risk communities. Key interventions include the deployment of GBV caseworkers and MHPSS staff to provide trauma-informed, confidential support at mobile and fixed service points capacity strengthening for frontline providers through trainings on GBV case management, clinical management of rape (CMR), psychosocial first aid (PFA), and survivor-centered approaches and operationalization Women and Girls Friendly Spaces (WGFS) will be established or enhanced to provide safe, inclusive environments for psychosocial support, life skills development, vocational training, and GBV information sharing. Survivors and vulnerable women will also receive vocational training and startup support to strengthen economic resilience and reduce reliance on negative coping mechanisms. Emergency cash assistance will be provided to facilitate access to essential services, enhancing survivor safety and autonomy. Integrated SRH services will include CMR, post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP), STI treatment, and emergency contraception, supported by the distribution of dignity kits to uphold menstrual hygiene and well-being. Community engagement will be conducted through awareness campaigns on GBV, PSEA, and SRHR, alongside the dissemination of locally adapted IEC materials to reduce stigma and promote help-seeking behavior. Service mapping and protection risk analysis will ensure responsive, context-specific programming. To strengthen coordination and learning, the project will hold quarterly review meetings with GBV actors and a final government-led evaluation to assess impact and guide future programming. Continuous monitoring and post-distribution monitoring (PDM) will ensure accountability and evidence-informed adjustments. With a total requested budget of USD 300,000.00 the project aims to reach 110,909 individuals, including 70,705 women and girls identified as GBV survivors in the target districts. In the context of ongoing conflict and insecurity, this intervention is critical to restoring protection, dignity, and hope for crisis-affected women and girls. ltbrgtlt/pgt
